items.summary: Public bodies across the UK report being swamped by a flood of AI-generated correspondence, dubbed “AI clog” and described by researchers as “agentic flooding.” Labour MP’s-office caseworker Hollie Wickens says half their emails are now AI. The Information Commissioner’s Office found many authorities received more requests in 2025; complaint length rose from about two pages to roughly ten times longer, with one reaching around 200 pages. Employment tribunal claims opened by single claimants jumped 28% to 14,000 cases between April and June, leaving 70,000 open at the end of that quarter. Transport for London recorded a record 4,769 freedom of information requests in 2025-26, up 5% on its prior peak.
items.title: UK public bodies overwhelmed by AI-generated complaints

items.summary: This guide explains seven Mixture-of-Experts routing strategies used in production and the models that use each one, from Softmax top-k (Mixtral) to Sigmoid gating with aux-loss-free bias balancing. It states loss-free balancing cut MaxVio from 0.72 to 0.04 at 1B, frames sigmoid plus bias as the current open default for frontier models in 2026, and notes expert choice leaks future tokens in causal LLMs, with DeepSeek researchers measuring an abnormal loss drop of about 10%. It advises reading config.json fields before serving rather than changing top-k at inference. The piece is written by Marktechpost AI Media Inc., which promotes its platform and newsletter.
items.title: MoE Routing Strategies Compared Across Open Models

items.summary: The article argues that Tesla has not produced a successful new product launch since JB Straubel stepped down as chief technology officer in July 2019. It points to the Cybertruck, which it calls an epic failure: installed tooling for 125k units yearly yet sold only 70k over three years after spending $2bn on research and development while making just $100m gross profit, leaving a net project loss of around $2 billion. The author admits not fact-checking these figures but notes Tesla planned far higher output—up to 500,000 units. After Straubel's departure came the Model Y in March 2019 and later the Cybercab; no other major launch followed. The piece speculates on leadership dynamics without knowing why Straubel left or how much he influenced product development. It adds that whether the Cybercab becomes a success remains to be seen, and it carries uncertainty about Tesla's internal decisions throughout.
items.title: Tesla's Product Launches Since CTO Straubel Departed

items.summary: Traders claim they have been priced out of Liverpool's Christmas market after a new operator, Underbelly, took over running it. Anthony Grice said he was quoted £12,000 for a stall at St George's Plateau. Jeweller Alex Healy said her smallest hut would cost between £14,000 and £15,000, which she cannot afford despite the cost-of-living crisis affecting her customers. Council leader Liam Robinson met traders to understand their challenges.
items.title: Christmas market traders say new operator's prices are unaffordable

items.summary: Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event. High winds in parts of Colombia and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. During the previous El Niño cycle, productivity across its farmers dropped by 13% in the Dominican Republic, 22% in Ecuador, and 6% in Peru compared with the year before.
items.title: Latin American banana producers demand fairer pay amid climate crisis

items.summary: Samco Securities named ten stocks for the upcoming fiscal year, including BSE, Adani Power, MCX, TechM, HFCL and others. It relies on its rule-based approach with disciplined profit-booking and stop-losses, advising investors to follow risk-management levels as targets may change. For Adani Power it cites a record Q2FY27 quarter with 141.5 per cent profit growth, then recommends buying at Rs 186-192 with a target of up to Rs 318.85 over one year.
items.title: Samco Names Adani Power Among Top Samvat 2083 Picks

items.summary: A brokerage upgraded shares of Tata Steel, Hindalco and Power Grid to 'Buy' and raised target prices. Nuvama's estimate for Tata Steel was Rs 9,900 crore; the company reported standalone EBITDA of Rs 10,320 crore in Q2 FY27, up 9.6 per cent sequentially. Hindalco India, including Utkal Alumina, posted EBITDA of Rs 8,450 crore against an estimate of Rs 7,080 crore. The article was published on Nov 8, 2026.
items.title: Nuvama Upgrades Tata Steel, Hindalco and Power Grid Shares

items.summary: The successor to European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, who departs in February, is likely to be Dutchman Klaas Knot or Spaniard Pablo Hernandez de Cos. Both were nominated by their countries when she leaves office. Kyriakos Pierrakakis, head of the euro-area finance ministers' group, said Friday that De Cos currently leads the Bank for International Settlements and that the Eurogroup would review these candidacies at its next meeting on 9 November.
items.title: Two Candidates Compete for ECB Presidency After Lagarde Departs

items.summary: The American Food and Agriculture Pavilion opened at the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai on November 6, marking its fourth year. Organized by AmCham Shanghai and the US Department of Agriculture, it drew more than $650 million in deals signed on day one for products including sorghum, wheat, beef and animal nutrition.
items.title: AmCham Shanghai Pavilion Opens at CIIE with Record Participation

items.summary: The China International Import Expo 2026 presented semiconductor and memory makers alongside AI servers, framing the event as a single floor showcasing the industry from raw materials to advanced chips. Organizers say rising artificial-intelligence demand is driving new supply-chain activity, with global tech companies demonstrating how their operations in China connect to the wider Asia-Pacific region.
items.title: Semiconductor firms deepen China supply-chain ties at CIIE

items.summary: A report from the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society (CERDS) says China has built the world's largest renewable energy system. By end of 2025 global installed capacity reached 5,149 gigawatts; renewables hit 33.8% of electricity generation versus coal's 33.0%. In China it stood at 2.337 billion kilowatts, or 60.1% of total capacity, and China supplied 63.6% of global additions. CERDS president Peng Huagang noted coal power is shifting from dominant to supporting source as coal-fired generation fell below 50% in the first half of 2026.
items.title: China Leads Global Renewable Energy Expansion, Report Finds

items.summary: Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker concluded a visit to China on Saturday, during which Chinese President Xi Jinping said China is ready to expand practical cooperation with Austria in emerging industries. The two countries are celebrating 55 years of diplomatic relations. Meanwhile, Austrian companies continue expanding their presence in the Chinese market and seeking new opportunities for business development.
items.title: Austrian Companies Strengthen Ties With China Amid Trade Growth

items.summary: At the China Pavilion during the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai, visitors could take the controls of a CR450 high-speed train simulator. The console recreated the prototype's controls, sights and sounds so guests experienced the driver's seat without leaving the expo floor. According to China Railway, the CR450 prototype reached kilometers per hour on its test track.
items.title: Visitors Take Controls of CR450 Simulator at CIIE 2026

items.summary: Tong'an Bay, once Xiamen's largest urban bay and a fishing ground, suffered ecological decline from unregulated aquaculture and wastewater discharge. Around 2015, more than 40,000 fishermen transitioned away as operations phased out and tidal flats were dredged. More than 200 million cubic meters of sediment were removed, increasing tidal capacity by over 40 million cubic meters and improving water exchange around 30%. In 2017 Xiamen launched a coastal new town project alongside the Huandong Romantic Line, a 50.6-kilometer ecological corridor now a popular tourism landmark.
items.title: Xiamen Transforms Polluted Tong'an Bay Into Coastal Tourism Destination

items.summary: A few months after a John Galliano retrospective was cancelled amid backlash over the designer's past, the Costume Institute announced its next Met Gala theme as extraORDINARY: fashion and the poetics of the everyday. The gala is scheduled for 3 May 2027, with the dress code traditionally drawn from the exhibition theme. A press release says it will explore how designers rework familiar garments and commonplace materials such as jeans, T-shirts, puffer coats, paper, plastic and metal. Reactions are mixed: Dana Thomas calls it tone deaf and a missed opportunity to honour late figures like Dolly Parton and Bob Mackie, while stylist Marian Kwei describes the theme as clever and an interesting celebration of fashion design. Some commentators note its distance from Galliano's fantastical work. The article notes red-carpet precedents for denim, including Da'vine Joy Randolph in 2024 wearing an all-denim creation by Zac Posen, and Troye Sivan and Bhavitha Mandava at last year's event.
items.title: Met Gala Adopts Everyday-Fashion Theme Amid Mixed Reactions

items.summary: President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, with forming a new government after last month's legislative elections produced no clear winner. A statement from the president's office announced the decision following consultations with political figures including Netanyahu. Factions backing Eisenkot totalled 67 Knesset members versus 46 for Netanyahu. Both blocs fell short of a majority in the 120-seat parliament, prompting calls for unity talks.
items.title: Eisenkot Named to Form Israeli Government After No Clear Winner

items.summary: The Jillaroos qualified for a fifth consecutive Rugby League World Cup final, defeating Fiji 34-14. Despite an early scare with an 8-0 first-half lead by Fiji, Australia recovered to advance. The team will face New Zealand next Sunday in the decider at Lang Park.
items.title: Jillaroos Overcome Fiji Scare in World Cup Final Qualification

items.summary: A masked man in military clothing drove a car into Krakow's Main Market Square and opened fire on Saturday afternoon, killing six people and injuring 16. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an act of terrorism. The suspect, a 24-year-old Polish citizen with no prior convictions but a firearms licence, was wounded and detained after an exchange of fire. A two-day national mourning began at midnight Sunday.
items.title: Krakow shooting leaves six dead; mourning declared

items.summary: Luca Van Assche lost the Paris Masters semi-final to Ben Shelton, losing 5-7 6-3 6-4. The 22-year-old Frenchman reached his first Paris final since 2008 for a French player and will rise to a career-high ranking of 34th when Monday's rankings are published. He said the run gave him more self-confidence, knowing he can reach a semi-final.
items.title: Van Assche ends Paris Masters run with boosted confidence after semi-final loss

items.summary: COP31, the 31st Conference of the Parties under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, opens Monday (Nov. 9) and runs through Nov. 20 in Antalya, Türkiye, which will preside over the annual summit. The venue spans about 1.1 million square meters (11.8 million sq ft), organized around dialogue, consensus, and action under the theme COP of the Future – COP of Implementation. Official negotiations occur in the Blue Zone; public engagement happens in the Green Zone. Facilities include halls named after Anatolian landmarks, a Zero Waste Museum, butterfly garden, and 630 low-emission buses for participants, with roughly 27,957 security personnel deployed across five medical stations and seven ambulances to support emergency response.
items.title: Türkiye Opens COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya

items.summary: France have named a reshuffled 42-man squad of seven new players ahead of their Nations Championship match against South Africa, following a 54-17 win over Fiji in Lyon on Saturday. The selection includes Teddy Thomas's return after five years and Gael Fickou, who could reach 100 caps. Flyhalf Romain Ntamack is unavailable due to a left shoulder injury sustained during the test.
items.title: France call up seven players for Springboks clash with Ntamack ruled out

items.summary: The UAE National Guard said Sunday it rescued 22 people after a fire broke out on a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. The rescued Arab nationals were all reported to be in stable condition, according to Emirati authorities. They received first aid before being handed over to relevant authorities.
items.title: UAE National Guard Rescues 22 After Cargo Ship Fire in Gulf of Oman

items.summary: The Japan Coast Guard announced that the “Godzilla Megamullion,” a seafloor formation discovered in 2001, has been selected for the International Union of Geological Sciences’ list of 100 Geological Heritage Sites. Measuring about 125 kilometers long and 55 kilometers wide—roughly 10 times larger than typical—the site is believed to be the largest megamullion ever found and was registered internationally in 2021.
items.title: Japan Coast Guard Names Godzilla Megamullion Geological Heritage Site

items.summary: The South Australian government will introduce legislation banning councils from issuing ticketless parking fines after a camera car passes, requiring inspectors to physically issue tickets. The Local Government Association of SA said it was not consulted and argued the technology improves efficiency. Premier Mr Malinauskas said AI could still be used but any ticket must be issued by an inspector at the time of the offence.
items.title: SA government plans ban on ticketless parking fines

items.summary: Talib Ahmed Bensouda filed candidacy papers for Gambia's December 5 presidential election, where incumbent Adama Barrow seeks a third term. The move follows a government report accusing the former Kanifing mayor of financial improprieties and abuse of office; his UNITE party rejected these as political manoeuvring and blamed the NPP government on national blackouts that have fueled protests.
items.title: Gambian opposition leader files for presidential election amid abuse allegations

items.summary: At 80, British designer Paul Smith spent a Saturday afternoon helping visitors at the Mayfair store of his label. He attended to guests from Norway, Greece, Canada and Mexico without revealing himself as the famous designer. The interview coincides with the publication of his memoir Threads: My Life in Style, which he frames less as nostalgia than as proof that old-fashioned success is still possible through hard work and curiosity. Smith says his partner Pauline raised his standards on quality. He notes that since air conditioning and travel introduced lighter Spanish and Italian fabrics, British style has become more international while keeping a playful accent. His empire now spans 130 stores, including 20 in Japan, employs more than 1,200 people, and posted earnings of more than €235 million ($264 million) in its most profitable year.
items.title: Paul Smith, at 80, still serves shoppers in his London flagship

items.summary: Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus and Anduril Industries, and Ben Lamm, founder of Colossal Biosciences, have formed a new company called Warhound. According to the Financial Times, reported through EL PAÍS USA Edition, the venture aims to combine genetic-engineering expertise with defense technology to design, breed and train canine units for military, law-enforcement and emergency-response teams, reducing reliance on dogs bred in Europe. The company is reportedly valued at $1.2 billion after raising $200 million in seed funding. Neither founder will run the firm daily; David Spirk has been recruited as chief executive officer.
items.title: Luckey and Lamm Launch Warhound to Build Elite Military Dogs

items.summary: After Republicans lost control of the House and Senate plus governorships and state legislatures, including red states like Texas and Kansas where they had long held power, analysts describe a shattered coalition that powered Donald Trump to three straight nominations. Outgoing Florida Governor Ron DeSantis called it close to an extinction-level event for the party, while Vice-President JD Vance blamed public anger over the war with Iran and predicted infighting. A New York Times analysis of voter data found Latino support for Democratic candidates rose 29 percentage points from 2024-26, and young voters aged 18-29 increased by 33 points. Strategists say it is too early to tell which faction will win out ahead of 2028.
items.title: Republicans Reassess After Trump Coalition Collapse in Midterms

items.summary:
The burned-out ruins of Kehlsteinhaus, known as the Eagle's Nest and built by the Nazis in 1938, sit high in the German Alps near Berchtesgaden. Gutted last month in a suspected arson attack on 23 October, the site has sparked debate about Germany's Nazi past amid rising far-right sentiment. Some argue it should be destroyed and returned to nature; others favour rebuilding or reconstructing parts, wary of Neo-Nazi pilgrimage. Isabel Heinemann says full reconstruction is out of the question but suggests documenting remains and adding modern design elements. Bavaria's Joachim Herrmann and Markus Blume support rebuilding without taxpayer cost. A 33-year-old man with a history of mental illness has been detained on suspicion of arson. The authorities have not commented on motive.

visual null},
items.title: Germany Debates Fate of Burned Nazi Eagle's Nest Retreat

items.summary: Thiruvananthapuram cyber police booked an 85-year-old man, identified as Raveendranathan Nair of Thycaud, for allegedly sharing abusive messages about Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi in a WhatsApp group. The FIR alleges the posts were deliberately shared to defame both leaders. Police registered the case under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act after a complaint lodged on November 4.
items.title: Cyber Police Book Elderly Man Over WhatsApp Posts on Gandhi Leaders

items.summary: Apple Executive Chairman Tim Cook posted a festive photograph taken with the iPhone 18 Pro Max to wish people around the world a Happy Diwali, writing: "Happy Diwali to everyone celebrating around the world! May the light of this festival brighten your year ahead." The image, credited to photographer Gursimran Basra and featuring a glowing diya, highlights the phone's camera. Cook has repeatedly shared photographs taken by iPhone users for Indian festivals such as Holi, blending greetings with Apple's emphasis on smartphone photography rather than professional promotional material.
items.title: Tim Cook Shares Diwali Photo on iPhone 18 Pro Max

items.summary: Last month, Oracle told investors it will not raise more than $20 billion in additional financing for AI through fiscal 2030. At investor day in Las Vegas, CFO Hilary Maxson said the company also expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 and top $30 billion in fiscal 2029 as capital spending declines. Analyst Jacob Bourne called Oracle’s massive AI infrastructure spending methodical amid investor concern over its reliance on borrowing and share sales, noting projections remain ambitious and far from guaranteed.
items.title: Oracle Caps AI Financing at $20 Billion Through Fiscal 2030

items.summary: A 65-year-old man from Dharamshala, Kannur district, lost Rs 2.69 lakh after fraudsters allegedly hacked his mobile phone during a WhatsApp video call while he tried to return wrongly-sized footwear bought online, police said on Sunday. The fraudsters withdrew Rs 2,69,500 across bank accounts at different branches; the money could not be recovered and Thaliparamba police registered an investigation under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Information Technology Act.
items.title: Kannur Man Loses Rs 2.69 Lakh in WhatsApp Video Call Hack

items.summary: The International Energy Agency says India's shift toward renewable energy could save the country nearly $240 billion on coal and natural gas imports by 2030, according to IEA. The projection assumes fuel prices stay near their 2024-25 averages. Solar photovoltaic power may provide about 60 per cent of those savings, with wind power close to 30 per cent. IEA executive director Fatih Birol said India's experience could offer lessons for other emerging economies.
items.title: IEA Sees India's Clean Energy Push Cutting Fuel Import Bill

items.summary: OpenAI's CFO Sarah Friar told CNBC that the company will continue its US data-center expansion despite a Democratic midterm sweep raising scrutiny fears. OpenAI dropped non-disclosure agreements with officials and shared construction plans publicly to win community support. Meanwhile, $2.5 trillion vanished from markets on Thursday amid AI-sector selloffs, though OpenAI reported 70% quarterly business growth.
items.title: OpenAI Expands Data Centers Despite Political Backlash and Market Turbulence

items.summary: November 8, 2026 falls on the day of Lakshmi Puja, when devotees worship Goddess Lakshmi for wealth and prosperity. The page offers more than 25 Shubh Lakshmi Puja wishes, messages and WhatsApp status updates to help readers share festive greetings with loved ones as homes light diyas and decorate for the holiday.
items.title: Diwali Wishes Collection Marks Lakshmi Puja on November 8, 2026

items.summary: Festivals in India, marked by firecrackers, coloured powders, processions and gatherings along riverbanks, bring together large numbers of people but also expand their environmental footprint. Fireworks release particulate matter such as PM2.5 and PM10, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and metallic compounds including barium and aluminium; the concern is especially around fine particles that reach deep into the lungs. Dr Abhishek Agrawal, a medical officer at a government hospital, explains how exposure can cause coughing, throat irritation, breathlessness and worsening respiratory symptoms, with children, the elderly and people with asthma or COPD being most vulnerable. Pollution may persist after celebrations end due to low wind speeds and temperature inversions during the post-monsoon period. Beyond the lungs, pollution is linked to higher blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms and cardiovascular complications, plus headaches, stress and hearing damage from noise.
items.title: India's Festive Pollution Threatens Health and Environment

items.summary: Expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh said invitations for his daughter's grand wedding are being sent across India and Pakistan, saying political differences have no place at family celebrations. He would invite leaders beyond party lines, including Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav. The event comes as Singh faces a turbulent period after expulsion from the JD(U) with his wife Neelam Devi over alleged anti-party activities in October.
items.title: JD(U)'s Anant Singh Opens Daughter's Wedding Invitations Across Borders

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi revisited her early memories of celebrating Diwali in a conversation featured on video, sharing reminiscences about the festival's traditions and festivities. She reminisced that diyas lit nearly every corner of the residence, around the pond, veranda and pathways, while an idol of Lord Ganesh stood at the entrance where the family lit its first diya. Her daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also appeared in the conversation.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls Diwali celebrations with family

items.summary: The Gadag District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered Kittur Rani Chennamma Urban Credit Souhardha Sahakari Ltd. to repay two customers Rs 17,63,274 of principal stuck in fixed deposits, savings and recurring accounts after their repayment demands failed. The society denied deficiency in service; the commission rejected that objection for lack of evidence and awarded interest plus Rs 20,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 litigation costs. Payment is due within eight weeks.
items.title: Consumer Commission Orders Credit Society to Repay Depositors

items.summary: A Sunday book pick reviews John Gray’s 2020 book, Feline Philosophy: Cats and the Meaning of Life (Penguin Random House), which argues that cats teach humans about living well. The reviewer summarizes Gray’s six-chapter case that felines live by following their nature while humans suppress theirs, framing cats as morally superior because they lack ideas and remain untroubled by death. Gray is described as a long-time cat devotee who has owned the animals for more than 30 years. The review notes his historical examples of violence against cats and Eastern faiths that revere them, ending with his ten commandments on behalf of the animal.
items.title: Book Review Frames Cats as Moral and Existential Superiors

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath defended his sister after a viral video showed her running a tea shop, saying she was pursuing financial independence and living respectably. He said the 25 crore people of Uttar Pradesh are his family and that everyone should stand on their own two feet rather than beg.
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Defends Sister's Tea Shop Work

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it ran a two-month enforcement drive from September 1 to November 5, inspecting 56,431 establishments and issuing 10,047 improvement notices. It seized more than 3,270 metric tonnes of food worth an estimated ₹81.8 crore and suspended over 1,100 licences while cancelling 52 and sealing 314 establishments. The regulator said it would keep working with State Food Safety Authorities to uphold safety standards.
items.title: FSSAI Seizes Food Worth ₹81.8 Crore, Suspends Licences in Enforcement Drive

items.summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday took a swipe at Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao, saying “simply growing a beard does not make you look like Revanth Reddy.” He added that imitation would not earn KTR the trust of voters and compared substanceless posturing to a fox trying to become a tiger. The jibe is part of an ongoing Congress–BRS war of words over governance in Telangana, which has included allegations about irrigation projects and disinformation on Godavari water. There was no immediate comment from Rao or the BRS at filing time.
items.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy Jabs KTR Over Imitating His Looks

items.summary: Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman called ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina a 'convicted criminal,' convicted by the tribunal of crimes against humanity during the July-August 2024 uprising, sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Dhaka has requested India extradite her under their extradition treaty and will follow due legal process without emotion. Hasina fled Bangladesh for India on August 5, 2024, after a mass uprising ended her 15-year rule; an interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus took charge.
items.title: Bangladesh Law Minister Labels Hasina a Convicted Criminal and Demands Her Return

items.summary: The Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer admitted on Saturday that multiple Elector Photo Identity Card numbers were inadvertently generated for the same person during a special intensive revision of electoral rolls. The clarification followed a report by The Hindu finding 803 voter IDs linked to just 397 persons in Mahadevapura Assembly constituency, plus duplicate IDs across constituencies from pending deletion applications after migration. Officials said cases have been referred to district election officers for verification and remedial action under the law. More than 99. 3 lakh voters were deleted from Karnataka's final list published on October 27, with voter numbers falling to 4.
items.title: Karnataka Admits Duplicate Voter IDs in Roll Revision

items.summary: A 55-year-old scooter rider, Santosh Singh Chauhan, was killed Saturday evening near his home in Kalyanpur area of Kanpur when a speeding Mahindra Thar collided with him. The impact reportedly dragged the rider for about 25 to 30 metres before the vehicle broke through a residential boundary wall. Police reached after receiving information and registered a case following a complaint from the family, while examining CCTV footage; the driver's identity remains unestablished.
items.title: Scooter rider killed after speeding Thar collision on Diwali eve in Kanpur

items.summary: Priyanka Chopra shared photographs from her Los Angeles Diwali celebration with husband Nick Jonas and daughter Malti Marie Chopra Jonas. Posted on Instagram Sunday, November 8, the images showed Priyanka in a burgundy-and-gold strapless gown with zardozi work and traditional jewellery, while Nick wore an embroidered kurta set and Malti twinned her father's look. The actress captioned it as camera-roll favourites and wished followers a Happy Diwali; Nick reacted with a diya and star-eyed emoticon.
items.title: Priyanka Chopra Shares Diwali Celebrations With Nick Jonas And Malti

items.summary:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali with security personnel in the forests of Bastar, Chhattisgarh on November 8, 2026. He described it as the first festival since India became free from Naxalism and Maoist terror, stating that every district is now clear of the insurgency and crores of citizens have overcome its fear. Modi credited their sacrifice for ending the menace and launching new development in the region.

visual {
items.title: Modi Celebrates First Naxalism-Free Diwali With Bastar Security Forces

items.summary: A speeding Mahindra Thar, allegedly driven by a woman learning to drive, rammed a scooter in Kanpur on Saturday night, killing 55-year-old Santosh Singh Chauhan. Police said the three occupants abandoned the damaged SUV and fled in another car that arrived shortly after; eyewitnesses say it was speeding before crashing through walls. A case has been filed while police examine CCTV footage to identify the occupants.
items.title: Kanpur woman learner driver kills scooter rider on Diwali eve

items.summary: Prakhar Gupta argues India should focus on missile submarines capable of surviving a first strike, given reports that China has likely resumed producing bomb-grade uranium. Analysts note China's existing stock could arm roughly 670 warheads but may reach over 1,000 by 2030, raising questions about implications for India's nuclear deterrent.
items.title: India Should Prioritise Missile Submarines Amid China's Resumed Uranium Bomb Production
